title: Look Back in Anger

vibeProfile.oneLine: A furious young man rages at his wife and postwar England.

summary: In a cramped one-room flat, the articulate, seething Jimmy Porter rages against his wife, his class, and a postwar England he finds hollow and complacent. John Osborne's explosive play introduced the 'angry young man' and detonated the polite conventions of British theatre, making room for a new realism of ordinary, working-class discontent. Raw, verbose and furious, it captured the frustration of a generation and remains a landmark that split British drama into before and after.
whyReadIt: The play that blew up polite British theatre and coined the 'angry young man'. Raw, furious and era-defining.

funFacts.text: It gave rise to the term 'angry young men' for a whole generation of British writers.
